theory.heading: What Angular HTTP Client is
theory.body: Angular HTTP Client describes the methods and patterns used within MEAN Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Angular HTTP Client is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Angular HTTP Client matters
theory.body: Without Angular HTTP Client, systems built with MEAN Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Angular HTTP Client works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Angular HTTP Client follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Angular HTTP Client.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Angular HTTP Client
theory.body: Angular HTTP Client offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
